title: Azulejos Ceramic Tile Painting
description: The delicate art of hand-glazing white ceramic tiles with cobalt blue mineral pigments, introduced by Portuguese tile masters and preserved by Goan artisans.
history: Brought to Goa in the 16th century, azulejos depicted religious saint lives, historical maps, and family crests. Today, Goan artisans blend traditional cobalt blue designs with Goan flora, coconut palms, and local folklore motifs.

craftspersonSpotlight.name: Master Orlando de Noronha
craftspersonSpotlight.quote: Every tile tells a story of sea trade. When you brush cobalt blue onto raw glaze, it turns deep azure only after firing at 1000 degrees.

image.caption: Hand-painted Goan Azulejo ceramic tile plaque
image.author: Frederick Noronha

title: Kunbi Tribal Handloom Weaving
description: Traditional coarse cotton handloom saree featuring bold red and maroon checks, historically woven by indigenous Kunbi and Gawda tribal women for agricultural work.
history: Worn short above ankles for ease in paddy field farming, the Kunbi saree went through a revival movement led by Goan fashion historians to preserve ancient wooden pit looms.

craftspersonSpotlight.name: Devaki Gaonkar
craftspersonSpotlight.quote: The red check pattern symbolizes soil fertility and protection. We dye cotton threads with natural Madder root extract.

image.caption: Traditional red and maroon check weave of the Goan Kunbi saree
image.author: Archival Crafts Documentation

title: Goan Brass & Bronze Casting
description: Lost-wax and sand casting of ornate brass Samai oil lamps, Deepastambhas, bells, and temple ritual vessels.
history: Goan coppersmiths (Shet) held royal charters under the Kadamba Dynasty to cast temple lamps and copper plate land inscriptions. Their brass lamps remain centerpiece artifacts in Goan homes.

craftspersonSpotlight.name: Ramesh Shet
craftspersonSpotlight.quote: A true Goan Samai lamp must balance on five oil wicks. The brass sound when struck must resonate cleanly like a temple bell.

image.caption: Traditional Goan Samai brass lamp crafted by metal artisans
image.author: Goa Metal Craft Heritage

title: Bicholim Terracotta & Clay Crafts
description: Hand-molded terracotta roofing tiles, decorative garden pots, and Ganesha idols crafted from nutrient-rich Bicholim riverbank clay.
history: Potters (Kumbhars) of Bicholim have fashioned roof tiles (Nall) for Goan houses for centuries, shaping them over clay wheels before wood-firing them in outdoor kilns.

craftspersonSpotlight.name: Gurudas Kumbhar
craftspersonSpotlight.quote: When rainwater touches a fired terracotta tile, it releases the sweet scent of Goan soil. That scent is our heritage.

image.caption: Terracotta pottery and clay water pots crafted in Bicholim
image.author: Frederick Noronha
